root_idea.summary: The root centers on something being thrown or falling to the ground through an act of grappling or force.
root_idea.development: From this core come throwing down and being prostrate, wrestling, fallen branches and bodies, places of falling, and extensions involving paired or corresponding things that meet or fall together.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural صَرْعَىٰ is presented under the normalized singular lexical citation form صَرِيعٌ.

senses.definition: Fallen or prostrate on the ground.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural صَرْعَىٰ, describing people lying fallen after the destructive event.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw down or prostrate on the ground; also to lay low or bend down by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of a person or animal and extended to things such as trees or plants; the act, manner, or result of throwing down may be expressed by related nouns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Epilepsy or falling sickness, a recognized disease involving seizure-like prostration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical description also compares the disease with madness or diabolical possession, without making those conditions identical to the disease itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person afflicted with epilepsy or with diabolical possession or madness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the adjectival or nominal description of one affected by the condition, distinct from the name of the disease itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind, species, state, condition, or manner of being.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general nominal use for a type or condition of a thing, including expressions for having two distinct kinds or states.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state or condition, especially the condition of one who has been thrown down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used for a single act or episode of throwing down, but that eventive nuance belongs to the broader throwing-down branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Two camels alternating at the water, one arriving as the other returns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression reflects alternation between two heavily recurring groups of camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two alternating periods or extremities of the day, such as morning and evening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported applications include day and night, the forenoon and afternoon, and the periods around sunrise and sunset.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing corresponding to, opposite, or standing over against another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression صَرْعُ كَذَا for what is opposite or corresponding to something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either of two opposite conditions in which a person or affair may stand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom عَلَى أَيِّ صِرْعَيْ أَمْرِهِ describes uncertainty about which of two opposed states or outcomes applies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A like, equal, or similar person or thing; a peer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for two persons or things regarded as counterparts or equals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A strand of a rope.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete nominal use with a plural reported as صُرُوعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who is often thrown down or defeated by others.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term contrasts with the agentive wrestler or thrower and can describe repeated vulnerability to being prostrated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who throws down or prostrates opponents, especially frequently or vehemently; figuratively, one who masters himself when angry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The literal use concerns wrestling or overpowering opponents; the figurative moral use concerns self-control in anger.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To humble, abase, or lower oneself before another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form V construction used with لِـ or إِلَى; it denotes self-abasement rather than physical prostration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wrestle with another, each trying to throw the other down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal Form III construction denotes a contest between two parties; the mutual Form VI construction expresses the same wrestling activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overcome or prostrated by wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physical prostration, used of a person overcome by the effect of wine.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Slain and lying prostrate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended use of the word for one thrown down, especially in descriptions of the dead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drooping twig or rod that falls toward the ground; also a branch lying fallen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported use concerns a softened twig suitable for rubbing and cleaning the teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow whose wood has dried on the tree without being pared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical description distinguishes this reported use from a related term for a bow that has merely dried.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A whip from which nothing has been pared.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized material description parallel to the reported use for an unpared bow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place of throwing down or prostrating on the ground; a place of slaughter by extension.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The locative noun may denote the place where people fall or are thrown down, and metaphorically the place where a group is slaughtered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Either leaf or half of a folding door or comparable curtain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dual مِصْرَاعَانِ denotes the two leaves meeting at the entrance; the sense is extended from the idea of two parts falling or meeting together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hemistich of poetry; in a narrower construction, one of the two rhyming halves of a verse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The poetic term is derived by comparison with the two leaves of a folding door.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Transitive throwing down and related physical extensions.
Making a doorway with two leaves.

Inflectional description of the verbal noun.

State or condition, especially of one prostrated.
Prostrate or thrown down, with plural صرعى.

Passive form illustrated with slain persons.
One who wrestles to throw another down.

cautions: The sole Quranic form is the plural صَرْعَىٰ; the public headword صَرِيعٌ is its normalized singular lexical citation form.

The Quranic sense is the general state of being fallen or prostrate; the separately listed meanings for epilepsy, slaughter, intoxication, and other extensions are broader Classical Arabic uses and are not assigned to the Quranic occurrence.
